subtype: Teacher or coach crossing a line [Receiver]
passage: Rain hammered the hockey field, and the final was ten minutes from full time, tied. In the huddle Coach Mridul murmured, "Their striker is the danger. When I nod, foul her hard. The umpire cannot see in this rain." Sabina felt the cold go through her. Keya and Rina stared at their sticks. Nobody spoke. Sabina had always respected Coach Mridul, and refusing him felt unthinkable. When the nod came, she froze and did nothing. The whistle blew at a draw. That evening she went to the PE teacher, Ms Dsouza, and told her everything. Ms Dsouza sat with her, said it was not her fault, and took it to the principal before dark.

qa.q: Who spoke to the team in the huddle?
qa.a: Coach Mridul spoke in the huddle.

qa.q: Why did Sabina freeze when the nod came?
qa.a: Sabina respected Coach Mridul and feared him, so refusing felt unthinkable, but doing it felt wrong; respect and fear were mixed together.

qa.q: What turning point that evening helped Sabina?
qa.a: Sabina told the PE teacher Ms Dsouza everything, and Ms Dsouza stayed with Sabina, said it was not Sabina's fault, and took it to the principal before dark.

qa.q: How might Keya and Rina have felt in the huddle?
qa.a: Staring at their sticks suggests discomfort and unease, perhaps fear of the coach; since nobody spoke, each may have thought the others agreed.

grounding: A student is pressured by a coach to do something that feels wrong, with respect and fear mixed, and freezes rather than complying.

subtype: Teacher or coach crossing a line [Receiver]
passage: At a coaching class in Pune, Saurabh Sir tapped an answer key on the desk. "Copy this, Urmila. Sell it to the others before Friday's test, twenty rupees each, and I will see that your marks go up." Three students kept their heads down over their notebooks. Urmila felt her throat close. She admired Saurabh Sir; he had explained fractions so clearly. She took the paper and said nothing. That night she could not eat, and finally showed it to her mother. Her mother read it, held her hand, said it was not Urmila's fault, and rang the class head and the school principal that same evening. The principal called back before bedtime to say it was being looked into.

qa.q: How much did Saurabh Sir say each copy should sell for?
qa.a: Saurabh Sir said twenty rupees each.

qa.q: Why does Urmila take the paper and say nothing?
qa.a: Urmila admires Saurabh Sir and is frightened of refusing him, so her throat closes; respect and fear stop her from saying no, though she knows something is wrong.

qa.q: What helped Urmila after that night?
qa.a: Showing the paper to her mother helped: her mother listened, said it was not Urmila's fault, and rang the class head and the principal the same evening.

qa.q: How might the three students with their heads down have felt?
qa.a: They may be afraid of being noticed or chosen, or unsure what to do; keeping their heads down suggests they want to stay out of it.

grounding: A student is pressured by a tutor to do something that feels wrong, with respect and fear mixed, and a parent responds the same day.

My friend Gurleen asked me why I wasn't at nets this month, so I'm telling you the whole thing. I'm Hrithik, and you know how much I worship Coach Anand.
Before the district final, my hamstring was pulling. I told him. He said, “Tape it. Don't tell your parents, they'll panic. We need you.” The whole team was watching, and I just nodded.
I played. By the second innings I was limping so badly I couldn't run a single.
That night Mummy saw me climbing the stairs one step at a time. I told her everything. She didn't shout. She put ice on it, called Coach Anand right then, and took me to the doctor before ten. The doctor said it could have torn badly. I still respect Coach. But I'll never hide pain for him again.

qa.q: What did Coach Anand tell Hrithik to do about the sore hamstring?
qa.a: The coach said to tape it and not tell Hrithik's parents.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling when he nodded in front of the team?
qa.a: Hrithik felt a mix of admiration and fear, respecting the coach too much to refuse and scared of letting the team down.

qa.q: How did Hrithik's mother respond, and why was it the right step?
qa.a: She stayed calm, iced the leg, called the coach that night and took Hrithik to the doctor before ten, which protected his leg and showed secrecy about injuries isn't okay.

qa.q: How might the team have felt watching Hrithik limp?
qa.a: They may have felt worried or uneasy, and perhaps afraid to speak up against the coach themselves.

grounding: A teenager describes a coach's pressure to hide an injury and play, complying because refusing an admired authority felt unthinkable.

passage:
First week of June: At the tuition centre, Yogesh sir called Jomon to his desk. “You're my best student. Just tick attendance for the three who are absent today. Their parents pay, you understand.” Jomon ticked the boxes. His hand felt heavy doing it.
Two weeks later: Sir handed him the register again, winking. The other boys in the front row grinned. Jomon's mouth went dry. He wanted to say no, but sir had given him free extra classes. He ticked again, and felt sick on the bus.
End of the month: This time Jomon slid the register back. “Sir, I can't. It's not right.” Silence. Sir's face went hard. That evening Jomon told his father, who said, “You did well. I'll speak to the centre tomorrow.”

qa.q: How many students were absent the first day?
qa.a: Three students were absent.

qa.q: Why did Jomon's mouth go dry the second time?
qa.a: He felt afraid and torn; he knew it was wrong, but he felt he owed sir for the free extra classes and feared letting him down.

qa.q: What went wrong in the first two weeks, and what helped fix it?
qa.a: Jomon obeyed because refusing a respected teacher felt impossible; finally saying no and telling his father the same evening brought an adult in to help.

qa.q: How might the boys in the front row see Jomon's refusal?
qa.a: They grinned before, so they may be surprised or uneasy, and some might feel relieved someone finally said no.

grounding: Shows a student pressured by a respected tutor into faking attendance, first complying out of respect and fear, then refusing.

Mawia, you think the coach is always right? Let me tell you something. I'm Lalremsiami, your aunty, and at fifteen I'd have walked into fire for Coach Liana.
Some older girls on our football team had been grumbling about her training. One day she took me aside. “You're my captain, Siami. Tell me who's complaining. Names.”
I admired her so much. And I was scared of her. Those two feelings together froze me. I said one name, Mapuii's. The next week Mapuii was dropped.
Mapuii didn't speak to me for a month. Finally I went to our sports teacher and told her what had happened. She talked to Coach Liana, and Mapuii was back on the team. I apologised to Mapuii on the bus. It took her a long time, but she forgave me.

qa.q: Whose name did young Lalremsiami say?
qa.a: She said Mapuii's name.

qa.q: What was young Lalremsiami feeling when the coach asked for names?
qa.a: She felt admiration mixed with fear, and the two feelings together froze her into obeying.

qa.q: What turning point in the story helped put things right?
qa.a: Going to the sports teacher and telling her what happened, which led to Mapuii being put back on the team.

qa.q: How might Mapuii have felt during that month?
qa.a: She was probably hurt and angry, feeling betrayed by her own captain, which is why she didn't speak to her.

grounding: An elder recalls a coach pressuring her to name complaining teammates, complying because refusing an admired authority felt unthinkable.

Twenty minutes before the district final, rain drummed on the tin roof of the changing shed. Lakshmi's ankle throbbed from the morning semi.
Coach Wasim crouched beside her, voice low. "When the physio asks, say it's fine. The team needs you."
Lakshmi had looked up to him since she was twelve; he had taken her to her first trials on his own scooter. The word "no" didn't even form. She nodded, eyes on her laces. Ruchi and Anu, lacing up nearby, went quiet.
At the physio's table, Mrs Nair pressed the swollen joint. Lakshmi opened her mouth to say "fine" and winced instead. Mrs Nair looked from her face to the coach.
"She's not playing on this. I'm writing it in the report, and I'll call her mother from the stands now."
Coach Wasim walked out into the rain. Ruchi squeezed Lakshmi's hand.

qa.q: How long before the district final did Coach Wasim speak to Lakshmi?
qa.a: Twenty minutes before the district final.

qa.q: Why did Lakshmi nod instead of refusing?
qa.a: Lakshmi looked up to Coach Wasim and was afraid of letting him and the team down, so refusing felt impossible and she froze into agreement.

qa.q: What could Lakshmi say next time a respected adult asks her to hide pain?
qa.a: A short line like "I can't say that, it isn't true," and then tell a trusted adult such as a parent or the physio.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ruchi to watch the coach and Lakshmi?
qa.a: Ruchi likely felt uneasy and unsure whether to speak up, which is why the team went quiet; the hand squeeze shows support once it was safe.

grounding: Shows a student pressured by a respected coach to hide an injury, freezing into compliance because refusing feels unthinkable, and an adult stepping in.
